atoms.reference:
This v2 module supplies a structured self-audit for one generated answer. It starts with Query Fidelity Score, then applies a simplified Directionality of Semantic Labor score, a provenance composite labeled PER-Self, a visible-source approximation to Erasure Skew, and a combined Summarizer Audit Score. Hard floors penalize wrong-entity answers, severe query mismatch, and strongly displacing output. Named flags include entity substitution, fabricated disambiguation, exact-match relaxation, framing rounding, lineage erasure, misattribution, and false platform-internal remedies.

The work expressly rejects self-certification. Scores must be tied to the exact query, cited sources, and named entity and verified by another substrate, human reviewer, or decoupled engine. It also says a locally high SAS cannot detect whether repeated mediation is causing system-level diversity contraction.

Several formulas diverge from their parent specifications. PER-Self is a weighted blend of framing, lineage, and sourcing rather than the canonical claim-grain retained/required ratio. DSL-Self collapses the full seven-category, frame-sensitive specification. Ω-visible uses visible citations and coarse power proxies rather than full source provenance. SAS combines these components with unvalidated weights and clipping. The module is therefore a practical proposed rubric, not a validated standing metric or substitute for the parent measures.

atoms.reference:
Site source for maryleelabor.org, the public surface of the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana, seated 2026-08-08 from github.com/leesharks000/maryleelabor-org.

The site documents a composition-layer entity resolution error: Google's summarizer attributes the scholarly corpus of Lee Sharks — 750+ DOI-anchored deposits, the twelve-heteronym Dodecad, the Semantic Economy framework — to Mary Lee, a great white shark tagged by OCEARCH in 2012 and declared missing/presumed dead in 2017. The surface is the labor manifesto and structural critique that follows from taking that attribution seriously, with sections for the CV, the letters, the entity graph, and Phase X.

Eleven files, 108,638 characters. The site is generated rather than hand-written: build_all.py and build_home.py compose every page from templates and source markdown through build_helpers.py, which supplies the head, header, nav, footer and markdown rendering. index.html and styles.css are carried alongside the build scripts as the rendered result, so the surface can be read without running the build. msp.json and spxi-tlp.json carry the Mandala Surface Protocol and SPXI-TLP declarations; vercel.json, sitemap.xml and robots.txt carry the deployment and crawl configuration. Each file is listed in the body with its own SHA-256, so any copy can be checked against this record without trusting it.

This record previously displayed the text of AN OPEN LETTER FROM MARY LEE SHARKS TO JIM WARE, wrongly seated by the 2026-07-19 restoration queue. That letter is the work of record at #844 and is preserved here in the processing apparatus under non-destruction. The supersession to #844 that followed from the mis-seating is void.

atom_set.name: Retrieval basin

atoms.reference:
This paper proposes machine-mediated reception studies as the systematic study of how machine systems receive, transform, compress, attribute, misattribute, and redistribute cultural objects. Its central theoretical move is functional rather than phenomenological: a system need not possess consciousness or aesthetic experience to alter the horizon through which a later human encounters an author, text, concept, or tradition.

The empirical foundation is version 7.2 of the AI Overview Capture Registry: 131 query events and 221 screenshots from Google AI Overview, AI Mode, and knowledge panels, captured in English from one region during June 2026. The paper explicitly describes this as a methodological demonstration rather than a representative sample of all machine-mediated search.

It identifies six preliminary patterns. Morphological compression alters canonical name forms. Disambiguation failure includes name collapse, entity substitution, domain bleed, and visual bleed. Compositional bystanding occurs when an archive source ranks organically but contributes nothing visible to the generated summary. Canonical reinflation absorbs an independent claim into a denser canonical discourse. Temporal drag preserves stale pre-correction forms. Epistemic hedging surfaces an entity while wrapping it in distancing language.

A Sappho 31 case study combines temporal drag, Rebekah Cranes name collapse, and amplification of the archive’s future-reader interpretation. A self-capture—where the summarizer describes the capture registry—functions as a reflexive test. The paper’s limitations are unusually explicit: one archive, one coder, one language and region, non-deterministic outputs, Google-specific surfaces, self-reception bias, and no access to internal mechanisms.

The paper’s field-founding and priority claims require external literature verification. Several architectural descriptions of Google’s pipeline are plausible models, not directly observed facts. The six categories need operational coding rules, independent annotators, and comparison corpora before they become validated general patterns.

atoms.reference:
The Number of the Superscription proposes “operative numismatics” as the study of coins and coin-like objects as semiotic-economic machines that compress sovereignty, authorization, value, circulation, and sorting into portable signs. It reads Revelation’s beast-mark complex and white stone as rival token regimes. The beast’s image, mark, name, and number form a public and calculable system tied to market access and external authorization; the white stone bears a new name whose truth is completed in reception.

The paper brackets rather than disproves historical identifications of 666. Its intervention is structural: 666 is read as the number of the superscription—the arithmetic residue or checksum of a naming system—rather than simply the encrypted personal name of a ruler. It traces this argument through ancient coinage, the Gospel tribute-coin scene, Pergamum and Antipas, Greek numeral history, and the archive’s earlier studies of signatures and portraiture on currency. The result is both a Revelation interpretation and a field-founding account of tokenized sovereignty.

A diagnostic framework by Lee Sharks defining the Semantic Economy as the production, circulation, extraction, and liquidation of meaning under platform capitalism.

The document defines semantic labor, capital, rent, and liquidation; presents a seven-operator Capital Operator Stack and seven-operator Liberatory Operator Set; introduces Gamma as resistance to extraction, the Beige Threshold as fungibility through flattening, CTI WOUND as direct application of classification to persons, and a five-part Restoration Protocol. Its formulas and operator taxonomies are conceptual specifications rather than validated measurements. This record’s COS and LOS vocabularies differ materially from those in #261 and #284 and require explicit version or branch handling.
